examples.en: The company put a lot of money into the new business.
The coach sends in a new player in the second half.

examples.ko: 사람을 더 투입하면 일이 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: If we put in more people, the work finishes faster.

examples.ko: 소방대가 불을 끄려고 헬기를 투입할 거래요.
examples.en: I hear the fire department will send in a helicopter to put out the fire.
Check before you put the materials into the machine.

examples.ko: 시간을 많이 투입한 만큼 결과가 좋아요.
examples.en: The result is good in proportion to the time put in.

explain: 돈, 사람, 시간, 장비처럼 일에 필요한 것을 넣을 때 써요. '넣다'보다 딱딱하고 계획적인 느낌이에요. '인력을 투입하다', '예산을 투입하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 거의 정해져 있어요.

phrases.example: 회사가 새 일에 인력을 더 투입했어요.
phrases.en: The company put more staff into the new project.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 일에 보낼 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for putting people onto a job.

phrases.en: The city put funds into the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 계획적으로 쓴다는 느낌이 있는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing with the sense of spending money in a planned way.

phrases.en: We plan to send in the rescue team right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 보낼 계획을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression used to state a plan to send in resources.

explain_en: Use it for putting in what a job needs: money, people, time, equipment. It is stiffer and more planned than '넣다'. Common pairs are '인력을 투입하다' and '예산을 투입하다'.

examples.en: My friend is holding a solo exhibition next month.
I went to the painter's first solo exhibition.

examples.ko: 개인전에서는 한 사람의 작품만 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At a solo show you can see only one person's works.
He won the gold medal in the individual table tennis event.
This tournament is split into team and individual events.

examples.ko: 개인전 준비로 요즘 잠을 거의 못 자요.
examples.en: I hardly sleep these days preparing for my solo show.

explain: 개인전은 두 가지로 써요. 미술에서는 한 작가의 작품만 모은 전시회이고, 운동에서는 팀이 아닌 한 사람이 겨루는 경기예요. 반대말은 전시회에서는 여럿이 함께 여는 '단체전', 경기에서도 '단체전'이에요.

phrases.en: That painter is holding a solo exhibition in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작가가 혼자 전시회를 할 때 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for an artist holding a solo show.

phrases.en: This match is a team event, not an individual one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인전의 반대말로, 여럿이 함께 하는 전시나 경기예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 개인전: a show or match done by a group.

phrases.en: My younger sibling competed in the individual swimming event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 이름을 앞에 붙여 혼자 겨루는 경기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a sport name before it to mean an individual event.

explain_en: Gaeinjeon has two uses: in art it is an exhibition of one artist's work, and in sports it is a match where one person competes rather than a team. The opposite in both cases is 단체전, a group show or team event.

examples.en: The city holds a festival every year.
Do you know the country that hosted the Olympics?
The school will hold a sports day in autumn.
There's a lot to prepare to host a competition.
After holding the exhibition, it became very popular.
We held a small concert.

explain: 축제, 대회, 전시회 같은 큰 행사를 여는 주최자가 쓰는 말이에요. 작은 모임이나 파티에는 '열다'나 '하다'가 자연스러워요. 열리는 행사를 주어로 하면 '개최되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The school hosts a singing contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대회, 축제, 전시회'처럼 큰 행사와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs well with big events like contests, festivals, and exhibitions.

phrases.example: 시는 다음 달에 전시회를 개최할 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The city plans to hold an exhibition next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 열 계획이 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an event is planned for the future.

phrases.en: Our neighborhood opens a small market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 행사나 모임에는 '열다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For small events or gatherings, 열다 sounds more natural.

explain_en: Formal active; someone holds a festival or meeting (축제를 개최하다). Used by an organizer for big events such as festivals, contests and exhibitions. For small gatherings and parties, the plain verbs for 'open' or 'do' sound natural. When the event is the subject, the passive form is used.

dis.h: hold an event at a time or place
gh: oversee and run an event or task
be the official organizer behind an event

p.n: 주최하다 says you are the official organizer, not just that it is held.

examples.en: In college, I set off on a no-money trip with a friend.

examples.ko: 요즘은 무전여행을 하는 사람이 많지 않아요.
examples.en: These days not many people travel without money.

examples.ko: 무전여행 중에 낯선 아주머니가 밥을 주셨어요.
examples.en: During the trip, a stranger woman gave me a meal.
I heard my father even went on no-money trips when he was young.

examples.ko: 돈 없이 가는 무전여행은 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A trip with no money can be dangerous.
A trip with no money? That's really brave of you.

explain: 돈을 거의 안 가지고 다른 사람의 도움으로 먹고 자며 다니는 여행이에요. 돈을 쓰되 싸게 다니는 '배낭여행'과는 달라요. 요즘은 위험해서 드물고, 옛날이야기나 추억담에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I want to go on a no-money trip with a friend during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'와 함께 써서 그런 여행을 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '하다' it means doing that kind of trip.

phrases.en: I heard my father went on a no-money trip when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가다'와 함께 써서 그런 여행을 떠난다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '가다' it means setting out on that kind of trip.
phrases.en_equiv: to go on a no-money trip

phrases.en: The memories of the no-money trip are still vivid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 여행을 떠올리는 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when recalling a trip from the past.

explain_en: It means travelling with almost no money, relying on others' help for food and a place to sleep. It differs from '배낭여행' (backpacking), where you still spend money but cheaply. It is rare today because of the risks and mostly comes up in old stories and memories.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 겨울마다 제주도로 전지훈련을 가요.
examples.en: Our team goes to Jeju Island for a training camp every winter.

examples.ko: 야구 선수들이 따뜻한 곳에서 전지훈련을 해요.
examples.en: The baseball players do their camp training in a warm place.

examples.ko: 전지훈련 중에는 휴대폰을 마음대로 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: During the training camp, you can't use your phone freely.
This training camp takes place abroad for two weeks.

examples.ko: 전지훈련에서 돌아온 선수들이 많이 힘들어 보여요.
examples.en: The players back from the training camp look very tired.

examples.ko: 동생은 축구부 전지훈련에 참가하려고 돈을 모았어요.
examples.en: My younger brother saved money to join the soccer club's training camp.

explain: 스포츠 팀이 평소 훈련하는 곳을 떠나 다른 지역이나 외국에서 하는 훈련이에요. '합숙 훈련'은 함께 지낸다는 점이, 전지훈련은 장소를 옮겨 간다는 점이 중심이에요. 보통 '전지훈련을 가다/떠나다/하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The baseball team leaves for out-of-town training tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훈련하러 다른 곳으로 출발한다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses the idea of setting out for training somewhere else.

phrases.en: The soccer team is preparing for training abroad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 나라로 가서 하는 훈련을 말할 때 앞에 '해외'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 해외 in front when the training takes place in another country.

phrases.en: The players are in training camp in Jeju right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 훈련하고 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the team is currently in the middle of the training.

explain_en: It is training a sports team does away from its usual base, in another region or abroad. '합숙 훈련' focuses on living together, whereas 전지훈련 focuses on moving to another place. People usually say '전지훈련을 가다/떠나다/하다'.

examples.ko: 체조 선수가 평행봉 위에서 멋진 동작을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The gymnast showed an amazing routine on the parallel bars.
He won the gold medal in the parallel bars event.
I hang on the parallel bars and work out every day.
There are parallel bars in the park, so it's good for exercising.

examples.ko: 평행봉을 잡을 때는 손이 미끄럽지 않게 해야 해요.
examples.en: When you grab the parallel bars, your hands must not be slippery.

examples.ko: 오늘 체육 시간에 평행봉을 처음 해 봤어요.
examples.en: Today in PE class I tried the parallel bars for the first time.

explain: 체조 종목이면서 그 기구 이름이에요. 철봉과는 다른 기구이고, 공원 운동 기구로도 자주 볼 수 있어서 체조 이야기와 운동 이야기 둘 다에 나와요.

phrases.example: 공원 평행봉을 잡고 몸을 들어 올렸어요.
phrases.en: I held the parallel bars in the park and lifted my body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공원 운동 기구로 쓸 때 자주 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when using it as park exercise equipment.

phrases.en: Applause poured in when the parallel bars routine ended.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체조 경기에서 선수의 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a gymnast's routine in competition.

phrases.example: 평행봉 운동은 팔 힘을 기르는 데 좋아요.
phrases.en: Parallel bars exercises are good for building arm strength.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기구를 이용한 운동 이야기에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about exercising with the equipment.

explain_en: It is both a gymnastics event and the name of the apparatus. It is a different piece of equipment from the '철봉' (horizontal bar), and since you also often see it as park exercise equipment, it comes up in both gymnastics and workout talk.

examples.en: We held my father's sixtieth birthday party at a restaurant.
This weekend I'm going to my eldest aunt's sixtieth birthday party.

examples.ko: 요즘은 환갑잔치 대신 가족 여행을 가는 집도 있어요.
examples.en: These days some families take a trip instead of holding a sixtieth birthday party.

examples.ko: 할머니 환갑잔치 때 온 가족이 모였어요.
examples.en: The whole family gathered for my grandmother's sixtieth birthday party.
At the party, the son sang a song for his parent.

examples.ko: 환갑잔치 준비 때문에 요즘 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: I've been swamped lately preparing for the sixtieth birthday party.

explain: '환갑'은 60번째 생일(한국식 나이로 61세)을 말하고, 좀 더 격식 있게는 '회갑'이라고 해요. 그 다음 큰 잔치는 '칠순잔치'예요. 어른께는 '환갑을 맞으시다'처럼 높여 말해요.

phrases.en: We held my parents' sixtieth birthday party at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잔치를 준비해서 치른다는 뜻으로, '하다'보다 조금 더 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to host and organize the party; it sounds a bit more natural than just 'do' (하다).
phrases.en_equiv: to hold a sixtieth birthday party

phrases.en: I invited my relatives to the sixtieth birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잔치에 사람을 부를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when inviting people to the party.
phrases.en_equiv: to invite to a sixtieth birthday party

phrases.en: The whole family gathered for my grandfather's sixtieth birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: '환갑잔치'와 뜻이 같지만 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 환갑잔치 but more formal.

explain_en: '환갑' is the 60th birthday (61 in Korean age), and a more formal word for it is '회갑'. The next big celebration is the '칠순잔치' (70th). For elders you say it respectfully, as in '환갑을 맞으시다'.

en: sewing work; things to be sewn

examples.en: Every evening my grandmother sits down with her sewing.
The sewing has piled up, so I plan to do it all at once on the weekend.

examples.ko: 어머니가 바느질감을 한 보따리 들고 오셨어요.
examples.en: My mother came carrying a big bundle of sewing.
This piece only needs the buttons sewn on and it's done.
She is dozing with her sewing on her lap.

examples.ko: 가방에 바느질감을 넣어 다니면서 틈틈이 해요.
examples.en: I carry my sewing in my bag and work on it whenever I have time.

explain: 바느질할 옷이나 천을 가리켜요. '바느질'은 하는 일이고, '바느질감'은 그 일을 할 물건이에요. 보통 '바느질감을 꺼내다, 바느질감이 쌓이다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Grandmother took the sewing out of the basket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바느질을 시작하기 전에 가장 자주 하는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common action just before starting to sew.

phrases.en: I spread the sewing out on the table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천이나 옷을 넓게 펴 놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when laying cloth or clothes flat to work on them.

phrases.en: I've been busy, so a lot of sewing has piled up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 못 한 바느질할 물건이 많아진 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means there is a lot of unfinished sewing waiting to be done.

explain_en: It refers to the clothes or fabric you are going to sew. '바느질' is the activity, while '바느질감' is the material for it. You will often hear '바느질감을 꺼내다' or '바느질감이 쌓이다'.

t90.ax: She is dozing with her sewing on her lap.

examples.en: I put insect repellent in the wardrobe.

examples.ko: 방충제 냄새가 너무 강해서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: The smell of the repellent was so strong that I opened the window.
Before storing winter clothes, I should buy some repellent first.

examples.ko: 방충제는 아이 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep the repellent out of children's reach.
Does this repellent really work?

examples.ko: 벌레가 생겨서 방충제로 쓸 만한 걸 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: Bugs have appeared, so I'm looking for something to use as a repellent.

explain: 옷장이나 서랍에 넣어 두는 벌레 막이 물건을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 벌레를 죽이는 '살충제'와 달리 방충제는 벌레가 못 오게 막는 쪽이에요. '넣다, 갈다, 냄새' 같은 말과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: It's good to put mothballs in every drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷장이나 서랍에 두는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic usage: placing it in a wardrobe or drawer.

phrases.en: I change the repellent when the season changes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래된 것을 새것으로 바꿀 때 '갈다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 갈다 means to replace an old one with a new one.

phrases.en: My clothes smell like mothballs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방충제 특유의 강한 냄새를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the strong smell typical of repellent.

explain_en: It often refers to the bug-proofing items you put in a wardrobe or drawer. Unlike '살충제', which kills bugs, 방충제 is about keeping bugs away. It goes with words like '넣다', '갈다' and '냄새'.

examples.en: I packed a spare set of clothes in my bag.
If you happen to have a spare, please lend me one.

examples.ko: 비가 올까 봐 여벌로 우산을 하나 더 가져왔어요.
examples.en: I brought one more umbrella just in case it rains.
I made one extra copy of the key.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 여벌의 양말도 꼭 챙기세요.
examples.en: Be sure to pack extra socks when you travel.

examples.ko: 여벌이 없어서 젖은 옷을 그대로 입었어요.
examples.en: I had no spare, so I kept wearing the wet clothes.

explain: 입을 옷이나 쓸 물건을 갈아입거나 대신 쓰려고 따로 하나 더 마련한 것을 말해요. '여벌 옷', '여벌 신발', '열쇠 여벌'처럼 옷이나 신발, 열쇠 같은 물건과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 비 올 때를 생각해서 여벌 신발도 챙겼어요.
phrases.en: I packed an extra pair of shoes in case of rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갈아 신으려고 따로 준비한 신발을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shoes prepared separately to change into.

phrases.en: I left the spare key with my mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열쇠를 잃어버릴 때를 대비해 하나 더 만든 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An extra key made in case the first is lost.

phrases.en: Take an extra pair of socks with you.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여벌로'는 예비로 하나 더 준비한다는 뜻의 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '여벌로' means preparing one more as a backup.

explain_en: Extra item kept in reserve, especially clothes (여벌 옷). It is something extra set aside as a change or replacement, such as clothes or an item. It pairs well with things like clothes, shoes and keys, as in '여벌 옷', '여벌 신발' and '열쇠 여벌'.

examples.en: Mom flipped the meat with tongs.

examples.ko: 게가 큰 집게발로 제 손가락을 꽉 물었어요.
examples.en: The crab pinched my finger hard with its big claw.
I clipped the laundry onto the line with clothespins.
There were no tongs, so I picked up the kimchi by hand.
At the restaurant, I held tongs and grilled meat.

examples.ko: 이 집게는 힘이 세서 잘 안 떨어져요.
examples.en: This clip is strong, so it doesn't fall off easily.

explain: '빨래집게', '머리 집게'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 쓰는 일이 많아요. 게의 큰 발은 '집게발'이라고 해요. 아주 작은 것을 집는 도구는 '핀셋'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I hung the socks with clothespins.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨래를 널 때 쓰는 작은 집게예요. 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small clip used to hang laundry. The most common usage.

phrases.en: A crab has big claws.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게나 가재의 집는 발을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pinching claw of a crab or lobster.

phrases.en: I picked up the hot sweet potato with tongs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 잡기 어려운 것을 도구로 잡을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you grip something hard to hold by hand using a tool.

explain_en: It often takes a word in front, as in 빨래집게 and 머리 집게. A crab's big claw is called 집게발. A tool for gripping very small things is called 핀셋.

en: to dewater; to spin-dry; to dry

examples.en: Even if you spin-dry a duvet, a lot of water stays in it.

examples.ko: 세탁기로 탈수하면 몇 분 안 걸려요.
examples.en: If you spin-dry in the machine, it takes only a few minutes.
I spin-dried the hand-washed clothes and hung them up.
It's better to spin-dry sneakers only briefly.
Please close the lid tightly before spinning.
It's spinning now, so please wait a little.

explain: 세탁기로 빨래의 물기를 빼는 것을 말해요. 손으로 물기를 빼는 건 '짜다'라고 해요. 몸에 물이 부족한 상태는 보통 '탈수 증상'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I hang up the laundry after spin-drying it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ 뒤에'를 붙여 순서를 말할 때 써요. 빨래 순서를 말할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -ㄴ 뒤에 states the order; common when describing laundry steps.

phrases.en: Please don't spin-dry this garment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 관리 안내처럼 하지 말라고 할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A prohibition, like on a clothing care instruction.

phrases.en: If you spin-dry for a long time, the clothes get wrinkled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '탈수하다' 대신 '탈수를 하다'로 말하면 시간이나 정도를 덧붙이기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 탈수를 하다 instead of 탈수하다 makes it easy to add how long or how much.
phrases.en_equiv: to spin-dry for a long time

explain_en: It means removing water from laundry with a washing machine. Wringing water out by hand is '짜다'. For the body lacking water, people usually say '탈수 증상' (dehydration symptoms).

en: to perform; to conduct; to hold

examples.en: The school holds an entrance ceremony every spring.
We held a quiet wedding with just family.
City hall will hold a commemoration ceremony tomorrow.
It is the day the company holds its founding anniversary ceremony.

examples.ko: 비가 와도 예정대로 행사를 거행하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to hold the event as planned even if it rains.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들이 모여 제사를 거행하고 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: The villagers gathered, held the memorial rite, and went home.

explain: '식을 하다'보다 격식 있는 표현이라 '식', '행사', '의식' 앞에서만 써요. 파티나 모임에는 어색해서 '열다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Our school holds its graduation ceremony in the auditorium.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거행하다'보다 쉬운 말로, 결혼식이나 졸업식 같은 식에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word than 거행하다, used for ceremonies like weddings and graduations.

phrases.example: 마을 사람들이 축제 개막식을 성대하게 거행했어요.
phrases.en: The villagers held the festival's opening ceremony on a grand scale.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 화려하게 식을 열 때 '성대하게'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '성대하게' (grandly) when holding a large, splendid ceremony.

phrases.en: We plan to hold the commemoration ceremony tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 치를 식이나 행사를 알릴 때 쓰는 미래 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A future form used to announce a ceremony or event that is planned.

explain_en: Active, formal; hold a ceremony or big event. This is more formal than 식을 하다 and is used only with words like 식, 행사 and 의식. It sounds odd with a party or a casual meeting, where 열다 is used.

t90.ax: We held a quiet wedding with just family.

en: rice dumpling; sweet glutinous rice ball

examples.ko: 어머니가 콩가루를 묻힌 경단을 만들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother made me gyeongdan coated with bean powder.
Gyeongdan is chewy and sweet, so it makes a good snack.

examples.ko: 시장에서 색깔이 예쁜 경단을 한 팩 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pack of pretty-colored gyeongdan at the market.

examples.ko: 경단이 너무 쫀득해서 계속 먹게 돼요.
examples.en: The gyeongdan is so chewy that I keep eating it.

examples.ko: 명절에는 경단 모양을 예쁘게 빚어 봐요.
examples.en: On holidays, we try shaping gyeongdan nicely.
I put gyeongdan in a cold fruit punch and ate it.

explain: 영어로 딱 맞는 말이 없어서 'rice cake ball'처럼 설명하곤 해요. '송편, 인절미'처럼 떡 이야기에서 나오고, 화채에 넣어 먹기도 해요.

phrases.en: We shaped gyeongdan together with family during the holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 동그랗게 만들 때 '빚다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '빚다' is used for shaping something by hand into a round form.

phrases.en: The red bean gyeongdan is sweet and tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉에 묻힌 고물의 종류를 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The coating is named before the word.

phrases.en: If you put gyeongdan in hwachae, it's chewy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경단을 간식 말고 음료나 후식에 넣어 먹는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A way of eating gyeongdan in a drink or dessert rather than as a snack.

explain_en: There is no exact English word, so people describe it as a 'rice cake ball'. It comes up in talk about rice cakes like '송편' and '인절미', and it can also be added to 화채 (fruit punch).
